content-primary.$description: Use for main text, titles, and essential content.

content-secondary.$description: Use for secondary text, such as body copy or supporting content.

content-tertiary.$description: Use for tertiary text, such as metadata, placeholders, or helper text.

content-brand.$description: Use for brand-coloured text or icons to reinforce identity.

content-brand-high.$description: Use for brand-colored text or icons to reinforce identity.

content-on-brand-high.$description: Use for text/icons on high-emphasis brand backgrounds.

content-on-brand-low.$description: Use for text/icons on subtle or low-emphasis brand backgrounds.

content-accent.$description: Use for emphasis or highlights outside the brand palette.

content-critical.$description: Use for critical text/icons, such as errors or destructive actions.

content-caution.$description: Use for cautionary text/icons, such as warnings.

content-info.$description: Use for informational text/icons, such as neutral alerts.

content-positive.$description: Use for positive text/icons, such as confirmations.

content-featured.$description: Use for featured text/icons, such as highlights or promoted content.

content-neutral.$description: Use for neutral or non-semantic text/icons.

content-critical-on-color.$description: A strong background used for critical messages, errors, or destructive actions that require high visibility.

content-caution-on-color.$description: A strong background used to signal warnings or cautionary states that require user attention without implying error.

content-info-on-color.$description: A clear background used to present informative messages or neutral system states that guide the user.

content-positive-on-color.$description: A strong background used to confirm success, completion, or positive feedback that needs visual emphasis.

content-featured-on-color.$description: A strong background used to highlight featured, premium, or promoted content that needs visual emphasis.

content-neutral-on-color.$description: A neutral background used to present default or non-semantic content that carries no positive, caution, or critical meaning.

content-primary-inverse.$description: Use as the primary content colour on dark backgrounds.

content-secondary-inverse.$description: Use as the secondary content colour on dark backgrounds.

content-tertiary-inverse.$description: Use as the tertiary content colour on dark backgrounds.

content-brand-inverse.$description: Use for brand-coloured text/icons on dark backgrounds.

content-always-light.$description: Use for text or icons that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.

content-always-dark.$description: Use for text or icons that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.

content-critical-always-on-color.$description: A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on critical or error backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.

content-caution-always-on-color.$description: A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on cautionary backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.

content-info-always-on-color.$description: A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on informative backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.

content-positive-always-on-color.$description: A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on positive or success backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.

content-neutral-always-on-color.$description: A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on neutral backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.

bg-default.$description: Use for the primary background of screens and surfaces.

bg-subtle.$description: Use for secondary backgrounds, such as cards, containers, or inputs placed on bg-default.

bg-elevated.$description: Use to create a higher elevation background against bg-default or bg-subtle.

bg-brand.$description: Use for primary brand surfaces, such as key actions or highlights.

bg-brand-elevated.$description: Use for brand surfaces with subtle emphasis, such as secondary actions or accents.

bg-brand-subtle.$description: Use for elevated brand surfaces, such as cards or containers with brand emphasis.

bg-brand-high.$description: Use for strong brand emphasis, such as headers, banners, or high-priority surfaces.

bg-accent.$description: Use for brand accent areas, such as highlights or supporting UI elements.

bg-accent-subtle.$description: Use for background fills that need a light accent emphasis without overwhelming other elements.

bg-critical.$description: Use for critical states, such as destructive actions or errors.

bg-caution.$description: Use for cautionary states, such as warnings or potential risks.

bg-info.$description: Use for informational states, such as system feedback or neutral alerts.

bg-positive.$description: Use for positive states, such as success messages or confirmations.

bg-featured.$description: Use for featured states, such as highlighted or promoted content.

bg-neutral.$description: Use for neutral states that don’t carry positive, caution, or critical meaning.

bg-critical-subtle.$description: Use for subtle backgrounds indicating critical context.

bg-caution-subtle.$description: Use for subtle backgrounds indicating caution.

bg-info-subtle.$description: Use for subtle backgrounds indicating information.

bg-positive-subtle.$description: Use for subtle backgrounds indicating positivity or success.

bg-featured-subtle.$description: Use for subtle backgrounds indicating featured content.

bg-neutral-subtle.$description: Use for subtle backgrounds without strong semantic meaning.

bg-default-inverse.$description: Use as the inverse of bg-default, typically for dark backgrounds.

bg-subtle-inverse.$description: Use as the inverse of bg-subtle, for elevated surfaces on dark backgrounds.

bg-elevated-inverse.$description: Use as the inverse of bg-elevated, for higher elevation on dark backgrounds.

bg-always-dark.$description: Use for surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-dark-high.$description: Use for high-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-dark-medium.$description: Use for medium-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-dark-low.$description: Use for low-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-light.$description: Use for surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-light-high.$description: Use for high-emphasis surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-light-medium.$description: Use for medium-emphasis surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-always-light-low.$description: Use for low-emphasis surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.

bg-transparent.$description: Use for transparent surfaces or when layering elements.

bg-transparent-light.$description: Use for transparent light surfaces or when layering elements over darker content.

bg-transparent-dark.$description: Use for transparent dark surfaces or when layering elements over lighter content.

border-neutral-low.$description: Use for subtle dividers or low-emphasis element boundaries.

border-neutral-medium.$description: Use for standard borders and general element outlines.

border-neutral-high.$description: Use for high-contrast borders or strong dividers that require clear visual separation.
